result.description:
MedicalJobsAustralia.com     Data Architect





Job no: 944478

Work type: Full time

Located in: Adelaide CBD

Categories: Information-Communication Technology, Public Health, Research and Data Analysis




 

The Commission on Excellence and Innovation in Health (CEIH) - Clinical Informatics and Innovation Directorate (CIID) - SACCaN D&I (South Australian Comprehensive Cancer Network Data and Intelligence)

Salary: $130,046 to $134,956 - ASO8 - Full Time - Term Contract up to 12 Months

Overview:

The Data Architect provides strategic leadership in the design, development and governance of a complex, patient-centric enterprise data architecture, including a data lakehouse, multiple analytical platforms, and associated data integration and interoperability requirements. The role ensures that high-value clinical, operational and research data assets are usable, trusted, secure and fit for purpose to support the objectives of the SA Cancer Network.

The Data Architect interprets complex business, clinical and information requirements and translates them into conceptual, logical, and physical data architectures, data models and standards. Working collaboratively with clinicians, the CEIH Clinical Informatics and Innovation Directorate (CIID), solution architects and other stakeholders, the role ensures a consistent, interoperable, and standards-based approach to data design across systems, platforms and agencies.

The role leads the definition, implementation and continuous improvement of data architecture frameworks, standards, patterns, and best practices, including lakehouse design, data modelling, metadata management, master and reference data, and data integration approaches. The Data Architect provides architectural assurance to ensure data solutions align with enterprise architecture, agreed Digital Health and CIID standards, and whole-of-government data and digital strategies.

The Data Architect works collaboratively with delivery teams, customers, and stakeholders to understand data and information needs, providing authoritative technical consultancy and design guidance to inform solution options, platform adoption and investment decisions. The role ensures that data architectures enable advanced analytics, reporting, research, and insight generation as well as supporting patient-centric care models.

The CIID values innovation, excellence, collaboration, knowledge sharing, transparency, accountability, and respect.

The Commission on Excellence and Innovation in Health is committed to providing an inclusive workplace that embraces diversity and inclusion for all employees. We strongly encourage applications from people of Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander descent, culturally diverse backgrounds, members of the LGBTIQA+SB community and people who live with disability and-or neurodivergence.

We are committed to making workplace adjustments to provide a positive and supportive work environment. You are encouraged to let us know if have any support or access requirements during the recruitment process and beyond to ensure you can perform at your best.

The South Australian public sector promotes diversity and flexible ways of working part-time. Applicants are encouraged to discuss the flexible working arrangements for this role.

Appointment will be subject to a satisfactory Criminal History Check and appropriate immunisation requirements.

Job ref: 944478

Criminal History Screening Requirement

A 'National Police Certificate' NPC (also known as a 'Nationally Coordinated Criminal History Check' NCCHC) for employment involving no contact with vulnerable groups is required for this position (general employment).

A DHS 'Working With Children Check' (WWCC) is required for this position.

Immunisation Risk for this position is Category C (minimal patient contact).

SA Health Services are required to implement the Addressing vaccine preventable disease: Occupational assessment, screening and vaccination policy in the workplace.

Enquiries

Meredith Knowler
CANDI Program Manager, SACCaN Data & Intelligence
E-mail: meredith.knowler2@sa.gov.au

?? Location: Bowhill, South Australia
?? Employment Type: Full-Time – Fixed Term (12 Months)


Bowhill Engineering is seeking a motivated and detail-focused Project Assistant to join our team and support the delivery of major infrastructure projects through advanced digital
systems and production support. This is an exciting opportunity to work at the forefront of fabrication technology, helping drive a smarter, more connected and paperless workshop environment using industry-leading tools including FabStation and HoloLens AR. Specialising in large government infrastructure projects and complexity done excellently, Bowhill Engineering is powered by technology and driven by great people to optimise and build structures that matter.


About the Role
The Project Assistant plays a key role in strengthening quality, certainty and production flow by embedding advanced digital tools into everyday workshop and project execution. Working closely with Project, Production and Quality teams, you will support digital QA systems, production readiness, reporting and continuous improvement initiatives across the business. Through real-time data, visual verification and disciplined systems, you will help ensure fabrication is built right the first time while reducing rework and improving communication between teams. This role is ideal for someone who enjoys problem solving, technology, organisation and process improvement, while working in a fast-paced fabrication and manufacturing environment.


Key Responsibilities & Requirements
-Support and maintain digital QA systems including FabStation and HoloLens AR
-Assist with production readiness, work packs and planning coordination
-Ensure real-time production and QA data is accurate and up to date
-Support workshop teams with clear and accessible project information
-Monitor planned versus actual production performance and reporting
-Assist with compliance tracking, reporting and system updates
-Identify opportunities for improvement and help implement smarter processes
-Work collaboratively across Project, Production and Quality teams
-Help strengthen transparency, communication and workflow efficiency across projects
-Support continuous improvement initiatives and maintain OFI registers

Experience & Qualifications
-Current Driver’s Licence (Manual)
-Experience in steel fabrication, construction or manufacturing environments (desirable)
-Strong organisational and time management skills
-Excellent written and verbal communication skills
-Competent IT skills including MS Word, Excel & Outlook
-Experience with production software, Tekla or MS Project (desirable)
-Ability to read and interpret engineering drawings
-Strong attention to detail and problem-solving ability
-Understanding of WHS requirements and safe work practices

What We Offer
-Opportunity to work on major infrastructure projects of national significance
-Exposure to advanced digital fabrication and QA technology
-Career growth opportunities into a Production Systems Analyst role
-Supportive and collaborative team environment
-Employee Assistance Program (EAP)Employee Health Assistance
-Active Social Club and strong workplace culture
-Modern workplace with multiple workshops on site
-Enjoy the River Murray lifestyle
-Join an Employer of Choice in the Murraylands

About Us
Based in Bowhill, South Australia (90 mins from Adelaide, 40 mins from Murray Bridge, 30 mins from Mannum), Bowhill Engineering has built a national reputation for delivering large, complex steel structures with precision and pride — all from one location.
Apply Now - Bring your confidence in new technology & software, your analytical skills, quality focus & ability to capture, interpret & measure production data - we have an immediate spot waiting for you!
Submit your cover letter, resume, and three references via the Bowhill Engineering website.
For more information, contact HR Manager, Samantha Krollig on (08) 8570 4208.

result.description: Zenith Vinyl Pty Ltd  Zenith Vinyl Pty Ltd is seeking a skilled Metal Machinist (First Class) / CNC Machine Operator/Programmer to operate CNC machinery and manufacture precision components. The role involves machine setup, machining operations, reading technical drawings, performing quality checks, and ensuring products meet required specifications and standards. Opportunities for career development and skills advancement.  Stable employment with an established Australian manufacturing company. Read and interpret engineering drawings, technical specifications, and production instructions.  Perform machining operations to produce precision components.  Select and change cutting tools, fixtures, and machine settings as required.  Conduct quality checks using measuring equipment such as micrometers, verniers, and gauges.  Identify and resolve machining issues to maintain production efficiency.  Perform routine machine maintenance and maintain a clean and safe work environment.  Follow workplace health and safety procedures and quality control requirements.    Qualification & experience   Relevant trade qualification in machining, engineering, or manufacturing (preferred). Ability to work independently and as part of a production team.  Strong attention to detail and commitment to producing quality work.   About Company    Zenith Vinyl Pty Ltd is an Australian manufacturer based in Brunswick East, Victoria, specialising in vinyl record production and precision-engineered tooling for the global vinyl record industry. Established in 2013, the company combines advanced CNC machining, engineering, and manufacturing expertise to design and produce high-quality molds, tooling, spare parts, and vinyl records for customers in Australia and overseas. With a strong focus on innovation, craftsmanship, and quality, Zenith Vinyl continues to support the growing global demand for premium vinyl manufacturing solutions.
